newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS confirms part-sale of Motor-Columbus.
newsitem.headline: UBS confirms part-sale of Motor-Columbus.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland confirmed that it was selling two 20 percent stakes in Swiss utility concern Motor-Columbus AG, reducing the bank's own share in the company's capital to 35.6 percent.

"UBS is selling the two 20 percent stakes for a total sum of 526 million Swiss francs ($405 million), with the price of a share at 2,600 Swiss francs ($2,000). This price was reached after an extensive and thorough valuation of the company and, at the time it was fixed, was higher than the share's value in the stock market," UBS said in the statement released on Sunday.
Motor Columbus closed on Friday up 10 francs at 2,730 Swiss francs ($2,100).

UBS confirmed it will sell a 20 percent stake to French utility Electricite de France International SA (EDF), and another 20 percent stake to Germany's RWE (Rheinisch-Westfaelische Elektrizitaetswerk AG).
The move must be approved by both Swiss and European authorities, it said.

EDF already said in an earlier announcement on Saturday that the sales of both stakes had been agreed. EDF said it had paid about one billion French francs ($190 million) for the investment of holding company ATEL (Aare-Tessin Electrizitaet, which is Motor-Columbus's main asset.
UBS's statement follows months of speculation about the future of its stake in Motor-Columbus.

The announcement also opens new perspectives in the energy sector, following a separate announcement late on Friday that Swiss industrial and energy group Elektrowatt was spinning off its energy activities, which will be listed separately under the name of Watt AG.
CS Holding, the group which includes Swiss bank Credit Suisse, holds 44.9 percent of Elektrowatt and has said it also wanted to sell the stake in the concern.
UBS noted that "for the time being" it will retain its 35.6 percent stake, allowing the bank to retain its status as the single largest shareholder in Motor-Columbus.
"By retaining this stake, UBS is ensuring the company's Swiss character," UBS said.

It said it had examined several alternative possibilities in connection with the sale, "and believes the solution it has chosen will create a strong basis which offers the best prospects for future success. It proved impossible to keep Motor-Columbus purely in Swiss hands. This European-Swiss solution creates the optimum prerequisites for exploiting the lucrative opportunities in a European energy market heading for deregulation," UBS added.
It said that Motor Columbus's stock listing would be unaffected by the move.
